sisg-bag-of-ngrams-model: Abstract p.1 and Section 3.2 p.3: the paper states its own model, a bag of character n-grams summed; read in context.
main-contribution-subword-skipgram: Section 1 p.1: the authors state their own main contribution, a skipgram extension with subword information.
skipgram-objective-definition: Section 3.1 p.2: the paper reviews and states the objective and the context set Ct it builds on.
binary-logistic-negative-sampling: Section 3.1 p.3: the paper frames training as independent binary tasks with sampled negatives and logistic loss, with the loss written out.
baseline-score-scalar-product: Section 3.1 p.3: the score s(wt,wc) as a scalar product of input and output vectors is defined, and the paper names it the Mikolov skipgram with negative sampling.
word-as-bag-of-ngrams: Section 3.2 p.3: the bag of n-grams and the summed scoring function are defined in the passage.
boundary-symbols: Section 3.2 p.3: the boundary symbols are the paper's own preprocessing, shown on the word where.
whole-word-in-ngram-set: Section 3.2 p.3: the whole word is added to its n-gram set; the her versus <her> note is in the same passage.
ngram-range-3-to-6: Section 3.2 p.3: n from 3 to 6 is the paper's own setting; the remark on other n-gram sets is stated as a possibility only.
fnv-hashing-of-ngrams: Section 3.2 p.3: hashing to 1..K with FNV-1a, and the word as index plus hashed n-grams, are stated implementation choices.
hash-bucket-count-k: Section 3.2 p.3: K is the paper's own setting. The text layer prints 2.106 (likely 2 times 10^6); the value says as the text layer prints it, so it does not overstate.
baseline-word2vec-implementations: Section 4.1 pp.3-4: the baseline is the C word2vec skipgram and cbow, except in Section 5.3; the quote spans the page break.
sgd-hogwild-training: Section 4.2 p.4: SGD with linear step decay and asynchronous Hogwild threads, stated with the schedule formula.
vector-dimension-300: Section 4.3 p.4: dimension 300 stated for both the model and the baselines.
negative-sampling-5-sqrt-freq: Section 4.3 p.4: 5 negatives per positive, probability proportional to the square root of the unigram frequency.
context-window-1-to-5: Section 4.3 p.4: window size drawn uniformly from 1 to 5.
frequent-word-subsampling-threshold: Section 4.3 p.4: the rejection threshold is the paper's setting. The exponent reads 10^-4 in the text layer; the value says as printed.
min-word-count-5: Section 4.3 p.4: words seen at least 5 times in the training set are kept.
initial-step-sizes: Section 4.3 p.4: 0.025 for the skipgram baseline, 0.05 for the model and cbow.
implementation-cpp-public: Section 4.3 p.4: C++ implementation, publicly available, with footnote 3 giving the repository. Basis is setup, not scope.
wikipedia-nine-languages: Section 4.4 pp.3-4: Wikipedia dumps in nine named languages, except Section 5.3; the list spans the page break and the quotes match.
shuffled-five-passes: Section 4.4 p.4: datasets shuffled, five passes.
similarity-eval-protocol: Section 5.1 p.4: Spearman correlation between human judgement and cosine similarity.
similarity-datasets-de-ru: Section 5.1 p.4: GUR65, GUR350, ZG222 for German and HJ for Russian are named.
oov-null-vector-vs-ngram-sum: Section 5.1 pp.4-5: sisg- uses null vectors for unseen words and sisg uses the n-gram sum; the names are defined there.
analogy-datasets-and-exclusions: Section 5.2 p.5: the A:B::C:D task and the four languages' datasets are stated, and questions with out-of-corpus words are excluded. It is a protocol choice, so the type should be setup, not measured; it is not a limit on a finding.
morphological-comparison-setup: Section 5.3 p.6: the model was trained on the same data as Luong, Qiu and Soricut and Och, as stated.
botha-comparison-setup: Section 5.3 p.6: Botha and Blunsom's model was trained on Europarl and news commentary, and the authors trained theirs on the same data.
data-size-subsets-protocol: Section 5.4 p.6: first 1, 2, 5, 10, 20 and 50 percent of the corpus, not reshuffled, nested subsets; the model and cbow are compared.
no-validation-procedure-for-ngram-range: Section 5.5 p.7: the authors state they did no proper validation to choose parameters, because test data is scarce. A caveat on their own work; the true type is stated limit.
lm-datasets-five-languages: Section 5.6 p.8: five languages, Botha and Blunsom datasets, about one million training tokens, same preprocessing and splits.
lm-architecture-lstm-650: Section 5.6 p.8: 650 LSTM units, dropout 0.5, weight decay. The exponent reads 10^-5 in the text layer; the value says as printed.
lm-adagrad-settings: Section 5.6 p.8: Adagrad, learning rate 0.1, gradient clipping at norm 1.0.
lm-init-and-batch-size: Section 5.6 p.8: init range [-0.05, 0.05], batch size 20.
lm-pretrained-vector-variants: Section 5.6 pp.8-9: three variants (LSTM, sg, sisg); the sisg vectors are trained on the task's training set to initialize the lookup table.
lm-two-baselines: Section 5.6 p.8 and Table 5 caption p.9: CLBL and CANLM are the two named baselines; the quote spans the page break.
table5-vocab-sizes: Table 5 p.9: the vocabulary-size row reads 46k, 37k, 27k, 25k, 63k under CS DE ES FR RU, a dataset property the paper reports.
table7-handpicked-illustration-limit: Table 7 caption p.11: the authors state the neighbors are hand picked, for illustration. A caveat on their own qualitative evidence; the Section 6.1 claim of better neighbors is not in this value.
ngram-importance-ranking-method: Section 6.2 p.9: the restricted vector without n-gram g and the cosine ranking are defined in the passage.
oov-vector-average-of-ngrams: Section 6.3 p.9: the paper states it averages n-gram vectors for OOV words in this analysis. Sections 3.2 and 5.1 say sum; the value reports only this statement, so it holds.
fig2-setup-one-percent-models: Section 6.3 pp.9-10: RW pairs with one OOV word, models trained on 1 percent of Wikipedia; the quotes span the page break.
abstract-nine-languages-eval: Abstract p.1: the authors state they evaluate on nine languages, on similarity and analogy tasks. Section 4.4 lists the nine languages.
conclusion-open-source-promise: Section 7 p.10: the paper states its own intent to open source the code; Section 4.3 footnote 3 gives the URL. A statement about the paper, not a result.
